failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the whole experience feel like a real production community app, not merely an implemented workflow harness?
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Replace all remaining generic action templates with domain-native product screens for each community workflow, with real object details, task-specific controls, natural alternate actions, and contextual result states.
visibleEvidence: Garden RSVP and plant exchange screenshots show domain content and natural actions.
Book nomination, book meeting RSVP, mosque announcement, volunteer signup, and export action screens still expose generic template copy.
Repeated sections named "Decision", "Details", "Other option", "Member outcome", and "Privacy boundary" read as implementation proof rather than user-facing product UI.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target personas?
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Vary layouts by workflow type: event detail pages, book nomination forms, announcement composers, donation receipts, volunteer shift signup, export package review, and inbox/detail screens should each have task-specific IA and content hierarchy.
visibleEvidence: Typography is readable and controls are large enough for mobile use.
Garden event and plant offer detail screens have clear primary actions.
Across the full matrix, many screens reuse large monochrome card stacks and status chips, reducing perceived product polish.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the experience community/product-centered rather than framework-centered?
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Audit every screen row for framework-centered language and replace it with community-specific nouns, details, relationships, and outcomes.
visibleEvidence: Garden Club screens include concrete community content: Spring Planting Workshop, Riverside Greenhouse, 18 going, 6 spots left, Sweet Genovese basil, pickup Saturday 1-3 PM.
Several non-Garden screens still describe abstract member forms, announcements, privacy boundaries, reviewer handoff, or export handoff instead of the actual community object.
The persona picker explicitly says "Preview the community experience", which is acceptable as local testing evidence but not a production member-facing pattern.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the whole experience feel like a real production community app, not merely an implemented workflow harness?
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Replace all remaining generic action templates with domain-native product screens for each community workflow, with real object details, task-specific controls, natural alternate actions, and contextual result states.
visibleEvidence: Garden RSVP and plant exchange screenshots show domain content and natural actions.
Book nomination, book meeting RSVP, mosque announcement, volunteer signup, and export action screens still expose generic template copy.
Repeated sections named "Decision", "Details", "Other option", "Member outcome", and "Privacy boundary" read as implementation proof rather than user-facing product UI.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target personas?
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Vary layouts by workflow type: event detail pages, book nomination forms, announcement composers, donation receipts, volunteer shift signup, export package review, and inbox/detail screens should each have task-specific IA and content hierarchy.
visibleEvidence: Typography is readable and controls are large enough for mobile use.
Garden event and plant offer detail screens have clear primary actions.
Across the full matrix, many screens reuse large monochrome card stacks and status chips, reducing perceived product polish.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the experience community/product-centered rather than framework-centered?
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Audit every screen row for framework-centered language and replace it with community-specific nouns, details, relationships, and outcomes.
visibleEvidence: Garden Club screens include concrete community content: Spring Planting Workshop, Riverside Greenhouse, 18 going, 6 spots left, Sweet Genovese basil, pickup Saturday 1-3 PM.
Several non-Garden screens still describe abstract member forms, announcements, privacy boundaries, reviewer handoff, or export handoff instead of the actual community object.
The persona picker explicitly says "Preview the community experience", which is acceptable as local testing evidence but not a production member-facing pattern.

visibleEvidence: Garden event RSVP action screen shows a workable interaction model with Going, Maybe, Not going, Maybe later, and RSVP to event.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material Design cards and lists
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Selection and voting pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy a nomination/voting surface with choices, current vote state, deadline, selected result, and meeting/discussion context.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Event detail and RSVP flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy an event detail layout: title, date/time, location, host, capacity/status chip, attendee context, RSVP action, and confirmation state.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Feed item and composer pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy a feed/composer structure: audience, author, timestamp, body, attachments/status, publish action, and receiver read state.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Form validation and review pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy a form flow with field labels, helper text, validation errors, review state, submit action, status, and protected-data treatment.

tickets.rootCauseHypothesis: The previous B25 gate let deterministic absence-of-known-defects stand in for semantic visual/product review. The visible screenshots still need a fresh LLM judge to inspect pixels, layout, content, and product fit.
tickets.targetExperience: A fresh LLM vision UX judge should be able to inspect the screenshots and state, from visible UI evidence, that the experience is modern, domain-native, and production-grade with no unresolved blocker or major findings.

concreteImprovements: Use the LLM vision judge screen reviews as the source of truth for what visually failed.
Replace any screenshot-identified workflow/test-harness surfaces with domain-native product surfaces.

implementationGuidance: Treat the imported LLM vision review as the independent semantic critique.
Prioritize screen rows and workflows named in `llmVisionReview.findings` and `llmVisionReview.screenReviews`.
Do not close the ticket until a fresh LLM vision review over after-screenshots passes.
contentGuidance: Write copy that matches the task: RSVP, donate, publish, approve, submit, review, search, export, transfer, invite, or reply.
Each primary surface should include the domain data a user needs to decide and act.
Use explicit alternate action copy such as Decline, Request changes, Change response, Edit, Withdraw, Cancel RSVP, Archive, Retry, Roll back, or Manage where the lifecycle requires it.
Use result copy that persists: Sent, Posted, Confirmed, Paid, Receipt ready, Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Claimed, Returned, Read, or equivalent domain state.
visualGuidance: Check hierarchy: page title, section headings, primary actions, secondary metadata, and result states should be visually distinct.
Check spacing and density on mobile: avoid crowded repeated cards, clipped text, overlapping controls, and weak touch targets.
Use consistent component styling and avoid default scaffold or test-harness appearance.

visibleEvidence: Garden RSVP and plant exchange screenshots show domain content and natural actions.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target personas?

visibleEvidence: Typography is readable and controls are large enough for mobile use.
